summary.text: The effects of climate change are the well-documented and growing changes that climate change brings to Earth's natural environment and to human societies.
Besides a general warming, they include shifting rain patterns, more extreme weather, more intense forest fires, thawing permafrost and desertification.
The effects vary in timing and location, and some can become irreversible once tipping points are crossed.

items.prompt: Suppose emissions are brought under control and surface temperatures stop rising. What happens to sea level rise?

options.label: It stops within a few years
It reverses and seas fall back
It was never linked to warming

items.explain: Ice sheets and oceans absorb most of the excess heat, so their effects accelerate and continue after surface temperatures stabilize.

items.prompt: A mountain wildflower is struggling as its home gets hotter. If it can shift its range, where would you expect it to go?
items.explain: Species escape heat by moving toward the poles and to higher ground when they can.

items.prompt: As the climate has warmed, how have night-time temperatures changed compared with daytime ones?

options.label: Both warmed at the same pace

items.explain: Night-time temperatures have increased faster than daytime temperatures.

items.prompt: Why is the ocean becoming more acidic?

options.label: Melting ice adds salt to it
It absorbs CO₂ from the air
Rivers carry in more acid rain

items.explain: The ocean acidifies as it takes up carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

items.prompt: Tree rings, ice cores, corals and sediments let scientists compare today with the past. What do they show about recent temperatures?
items.explain: These records show recent temperatures have surpassed anything in the last 2,000 years.

items.prompt: The Arctic has warmed faster than most other regions. What is the reason given for this?

options.label: A hole in the ozone layer

items.explain: The Arctic's faster warming so far is due to climate change feedbacks.
